sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (depends on Policy Schedule; examples show ₹3,00,000)

good.name: Pre-existing disease (PED) waiting period: 36 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: PEDs are covered after 36 months (3 years) of continuous coverage, which is within standard market range.

good.name: Specific illness waiting period: 24 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the Company.
good.reference: Section 4.1(a)(ii) Specific Waiting Period - Code Excl02
good.explanation: Named ailments are covered after 24 months, which is standard.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Section 4.1(a)(iii) First 30-Day waiting Period – Code – Excl03
good.explanation: Standard 30-day initial waiting for illnesses (accidents covered from day 1).

good.name: Room rent / room category: Single Private Room with A.C. (with proportionate deduction if higher room taken)
good.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a room where the Room Category is other than Single Private Room with A.C., then the Policyholder shall bear the ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses...
good.reference: Section 3.1(c)(i) Conditions for Medical Expenses – Room Category
good.explanation: Default eligible room is Single Private AC. If you choose a higher category room, associated medical expenses can be proportionately reduced (extra out-of-pocket).

good.name: Modern/advanced treatments covered (listed)
good.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person for expenses incurred under Benefit 1 ... through following advance technology methods: a. Uterine Artery Embolization and HIFU ... g. Robotic surgeries ... l. Stem cell therapy: Hematopoietic stem cells for bone marrow transplant...
good.explanation: Covers several modern treatment methods as part of hospitalization benefit, as listed in the wording.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: 30 days
good.quote: As Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses' during a period of 30 days immediately prior to the date of the Insured Person's admission to the Hospital
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 30 days before admission (linked to the same hospitalization claim).

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover: 60 days
good.quote: As Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses' during a period of 60 days immediately following the date of the Insured Person's discharge from Hospital
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 60 days after discharge (linked to the same hospitalization claim).

good.name: Maternity waiting period: 9 months (Joy Today) / 24 months (Joy Tomorrow)
good.quote: Claims will not be admissible ... until 9 months of continuous coverage has elapsed under Plan - Joy Today or 24 months of continuous coverage has elapsed under Plan - Joy Tomorrow
good.explanation: If you choose Joy Today, maternity waiting is best-in-class at 9 months; Joy Tomorrow has 24 months waiting.

bad.name: Restore benefit: Not available
bad.quote: Any Claim paid under Benefit 1 to Benefit 3, Benefit 7 shall reduce the Sum Insured for that Policy Year and only the balance shall be available for all future claims for that Policy Year.
bad.reference: Section 3(d) General Conditions applicable to all Benefits
bad.explanation: No restore/reinstatement mentioned. After a claim, Sum Insured reduces for the year and is not replenished.

bad.name: Consumables / non-medical items: Not covered
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – II to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.explanation: Consumables like gloves, masks, syringes/kits etc. (as per non-medical list) are out-of-pocket, increasing hospital bill burden.

bad.name: Mandatory co-pay: 20% for entry age >= 60 years (each and every claim)
bad.quote: The Policyholder shall bear 20% of the Final Claim Amount... *Entry Age means the age of the Insured Person at the time of issue of the first Policy... (b) The Co-payment shall be applicable to each and every Claim, for each Insured Person.
bad.explanation: If entry age is 60+, 20% of every admissible claim is borne by you, reducing effective coverage.

bad.name: Disease-wise sub-limits may apply if specified in Policy Schedule
bad.quote: For diseases or conditions or procedure that have a specified sub-limit then all related expenses shall be covered up to the sub-limit specified for that disease or condition or procedure.
bad.explanation: Allows applying disease/procedure sub-limits (if present in your schedule), which can cap payouts even when Sum Insured is higher.

bad.name: NCB / Renewal Bonus: Optional cover resets to zero on claim (forfeited)
bad.quote: In the event of a Claim occurring during any Policy Period, the accrued No Claim Bonanza will not be available in subsequent renewal, but in no case shall the Sum Insured be reduced.
bad.reference: Optional Cover – 1: No Claim Bonanza, clause 3.3(f)
bad.explanation: No Claim Bonanza is not protected: if a claim happens, the accrued bonus is not available in next renewal (effectively resets).

bad.name: Cashless network / cashless availability may be modified at insurer discretion
bad.quote: the Company may, in its sole discretion, modify or add to the list of Network Provider or modify or restrict the extent of Cashless Facilities that may be availed at any particular Network Provider.
bad.reference: Section 6.1.2(a) Cashless, point (iv) (as printed in document)
bad.explanation: Cashless availability/network can change; you should check current network list and cashless eligibility before admission.

bad.name: Post-hospitalization cover is only 60 days (not higher-tier)
bad.quote: As Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses' during a period of 60 days immediately following the date of the Insured Person's discharge from Hospital
bad.explanation: 60 days is on the lower side versus many policies offering 90/180 days; longer follow-up costs may be out-of-pocket.

unclear.name: Co-pay for ages below 60 / non-applicability conditions
unclear.quote:
Special Conditions shall be applicable only if the same is specifically mentioned in the Policy Schedule.

Special Condition 2 : Co-payment ... >=60 years ...
unclear.explanation: Policy wording shows a 20% co-pay for entry age >=60, but since special conditions apply only if mentioned in the Policy Schedule, confirm from your schedule whether co-pay applies to your policy and for which members.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
